entry.title: Could these 3 states be models for regulating AI?

media:group.media:title: Could these 3 states be models for regulating AI?
media:group.media:description:
Nearly-two thirds of Americans in a recent Associated Press-NORC poll said AI development is happening “too fast.” And as federal regulation stalls, Republican and Democratic-led states alike are moving ahead with laws of their own.
PBS News’ Tim McPhillips spoke with Will Clark, a fellow with the Technology & Data-Driven Governing team at the National Conference of State Legislatures, to explore how states are taking on frontier AI models, the most advanced general purpose models available right now. [5:16 PM]

entry.title: White House restricts lobbyist meetings with staff

media:group.media:title: White House restricts lobbyist meetings with staff
media:group.media:description:
The White House is tightening rules on how staffers interact with lobbyists.
A memo from the new chief of staff, Stephen Miller, says employees must first get permission before discussing government business with lobbyists on the building’s grounds.
A White House official told the PBS News Hour that, according to the memo, “staff are expected to dedicate their time unwaveringly to the working people of the nation.” The official called this “a much stricter process than before.”
Miller took over the role from Susie Wiles, who had come under criticism over her ties to lobbying groups.

entry.title: How possible end of military aid impacts U.S.-Israel relations

media:group.media:title: How possible end of military aid impacts U.S.-Israel relations
media:group.media:description:
President Donald Trump’s announcement that the United States will stop giving military aid to Israel reflects the “growing” consensus among Democrats and Republicans, Dana Stroul says.
Trump said earlier this month that the United States will stop providing $4 billion in yearly military aid to Israel. The current aid agreement between the two countries expires in 2028.
Stroul, director of research at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, told Nick Schifrin that the current period marks a “good time to pivot in terms of what the next chapter of the U.S.-Israel defense relationship is like.”

entry.title: Will a more 'insular' military lead to more 'forever wars'?

media:group.media:title: Will a more 'insular' military lead to more 'forever wars'?
media:group.media:description:
As fewer Americans serve in the United States armed forces, retired Army Col. Gregg Daddis says a more secluded military could lead to “forever wars.”
“If the armed forces become more insular, then those who are going off to war become more invisible to the larger whole, and invisible wars then have a tendency to turn into forever wars, in my estimation,” he said. “The less that war is seen by American citizens, the less likely they are to ask questions about it.”
Daddis joined Woodruff for her series, Crossroads: America at 250.

media:group.media:title: Remembering Gwen, 10 years later
media:group.media:description:
Saturday marks 10 years since the passing of our beloved colleague and friend, Gwen Ifill.
We, like so many of you, miss her every day. Ten years later, as we cover the news, we still ask ourselves one crucial question:
What would Gwen do?
